items.title: We Told TikTok About 100 Accounts That Sell Drugs: They Did Nothing
items.content:
We Told TikTok About 100 Accounts That Sell Drugs: They Did Nothing

Our investigation analyzed more than 500 TikTok accounts selling “tusi” or its ingredients, or explaining step by step how to make the so-called “pink cocaine” at home . We reported more than a hundred profiles to TikTok because its rules prohibit “showing, promoting or using drugs” and “providing instructions” for making or using them. In every case, TikTok determined that the accounts posting videos showing, selling, or cooking the drug were not violating its rules . When we reported the videos individually, as we did with 15 of them, TikTok removed them because they constituted illegal content in the EU; however, the accounts where they had been posted remained active, and other similar videos on those same profiles were not moderated by the platform.

The platform was not only unable to detect the illicit activity on its own; it also failed to address the problem when alerted to what was happening. This calls into question the robustness of its risk-mitigation systems and its ability to comply with its other obligations under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA).

TikTok (at times) acts against videos, but not against profiles

This particular account has just 13 videos, but some have more than 2.5 million views, and all of them show “tusi” being cooked. The author makes no secret of their intentions: they sell “cook packs,” offer “nationwide shipping,” and identify themselves as a “wholesale supplier since 2020.” It is just one of the more than one hundred accounts we reported to TikTok for violating its drug-related rules, and it remains active today because the platform does not enforce those rules. items.title: Linux Mint 23 is No More. A New Release Takes its Place
items.content:
In the project's September monthly update , Linux Mint lead, Clement Lefebvre ( clem ), says that the distro's version number now reflects the upcoming year and that point releases aren't a thing anymore.

Releases will come once a year, so 28 follows this one, and users upgrade from the current year's to the next. This ought to make it simpler for the many beginners who use Linux Mint as a gateway to the Linux platform.

The codenames change too, as the girls' names Mint has used since 2006 give way to boys' names. Linux Mint 27 " Adrien " is the first release to follow these new conventions, though it did not start off that way.

You see, the devs had no name or version number ready for the next release when work on it began earlier this year, so they picked temporary ones. This way, " Alfa " became the codename and " 23 " the version.

That was because the release strategy was unclear. The cycle length, the handling of minor releases, and the question of alpha releases were all undecided, and the strategy would also dictate how releases got numbered and named.

It all goes back to the January update , when Clem said shipping a new release twice a year while also looking after LMDE was leaving them with less time to actually build features.

By March, the team had locked in a longer development cycle and a Christmas 2026 target for the next release. The move we have been talking about so far marks the end of that long decision-making process.

Clem also points out that using the girls' names for releases all these years, from Ada to Zena , had made them run out of alphabet just as the schedule changed, which he found a funny coincidence.

He says the project has never spent a full year on one release before, and while the move away from six-month cycles was a tough decision, it is working out.

The longer cycle gives the team room to attempt projects that would once have felt out of reach. The Clockenstein project, which gave Mint a calendar app in the August update , now has an alarm app called Clocks too.

Alerts from Clocks run through the Clockenstein daemon and agent that already handle the calendar's notifications, so they go off even with the app shut. It handles repeating alarms and lets you pick your own sounds, while its look and behavior are borrowed from Android.

Three more projects, Superlight , Unfold , and Velocitty , are also getting their finishing touches. The next update blog will feature them.

If you need a refresher of the development work carried out so far, then you can read about Linux Mint's kernel removal feature and how Wayland support has been achieved .

Fire at Starlink site in Bulgaria after suspected sabotage in Poland

Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev confirmed on Wednesday that there had been a fire at a facility of the Starlink satellite internet service near the capital Sofia last week.

Two young men holding German passports have been taken into custody in connection with the suspected attack, Bulgarian media later reported, citing investigators.

The satellite network is a strategically important part of Ukraine's defence in the war against Russia's invasion.

The fire had previously been made public by the pro-Western opposition alliance Democratic Bulgaria (DB). Radev said he would not provide any further details in light of the ongoing investigations.

According to DB, 11 of 17 antennas at a Starlink facility near Sofia were deliberately set on fire on October 9. The antennas were used in the war in Ukraine, DB said.

Pro-Western opposition parties said they suspected Russia was linked to the attack.

Two men aged 20 and 21, both holding German passports, were detained in Bulgaria on Monday in connection with the suspected attack, several Bulgarian media outlets reported on Wednesday evening, citing investigators.

According to the news outlet Faktor.bg, the two suspects have migrant backgrounds and had legally entered Bulgaria from Greece through the Kulata border crossing.

The website reported that investigators were examining whether the suspects belonged to a larger sabotage network potentially linked to two men arrested in Germany earlier this week over a recent attack on a Starlink facility in Poland.

Bulgarian officials stressed that the Starlink facility near Sofia was privately owned.

Bulgarian Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev told parliament that additional security measures had been introduced at similar facilities, even though responsibility for their protection rested with their owners.

Plamen Tonchev, head of Bulgaria's State Agency for National Security (DANS), said he believed the fire at the Starlink facility was an act of sabotage.

"Such acts of sabotage cannot be ruled out in the future either," he warned lawmakers.

A fire also broke out at a Starlink ground terminal south of Warsaw on September 23.

Two suspected saboteurs accused of carrying out that attack in Poland were arrested on Tuesday in Nürtingen, near Stuttgart in south-western Germany.

The government in Warsaw suspects Russian intelligence services were behind the attack.

items.title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
items.content:
Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts

Ledger has confirmed that some of its devices distributed through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were compromised with a hardware implant that drained users' cryptocurrency wallets.

The company has been investigating reports of users losing funds from wallets purchased through CryptoBilis, a major Malaysia-based hardware wallet retailer operating across Southeast Asia.

Some researchers have shown the implant in Ledger X since September 16, saying tampered devices were available for nearly half the price of the original hardware.

Ledger wallets are physical devices designed to securely store the private keys that control cryptocurrency assets and authorize transactions.

On October 9, Ledger said it had launched an investigation into user reports of cryptocurrency losses and asked CryptoBilis to stop selling and shipping Ledger devices.

The next day, the company confirmed hardware tampering on at least one device, though it’s still unclear exactly how or when the devices were tampered with.

"Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger is reaching out to impacted users as part of the ongoing investigation," Ledger said.

The crypto wallet maker also noted that it was working with authorities to identify the perpetrator and bring them to justice.

“[...]Ledger recommends users who purchased a Ledger device from this reseller to not initiate set up if they have not yet done so. If you have set up your Ledger device, consider moving assets to a new Ledger signer (with a new seed),” warned Ledger .

Yesterday, Ledger provided another update , confirming that all user reports of unexpected fund drains were linked to devices sold through CryptoBilis and describing the affected volume as “limited.”

While the company did not disclose the type of devices compromised in this supply-chain attack, reports online talk about a spy implant in Ledger X devices that blends with the legitimate hardware.

Mark Karpelès, currently leading Karpeles Lab Inc. and CTO at Shells.com, showed a picture of the new implant in Ledger X, saying that it was "quite an evolution" from previous versions featuring manually soldered wires.

The former CEO of Mt. Gox said the implant was concealed behind the screen, but its antenna cable would have indicated that something was wrong.

According to Karpelès, the malicious hardware captured the device's display output and button presses to identify the seed phrase, then transmitted it to the attacker over an LTE connection using an eSIM.

"Ledger Nano X are used to store crypto. The spy implants are used to steal whatever crypto you store in those Ledger Nano X," Karpelès explained .

Although the CEO did not name CryptoBilis as the vendor of the compromised LedgerX, he said the device was not purchased via Ledger's recommended channels but from "a well known platform via a Chinese seller (product shipped from Malaysia)."

Tibane Labs, a cryptocurrency research and development studio, confirmed Karpelès' finding, adding that there were two implant versions for Ledger X.

The researchers obtained two variants, one in a Ledger device bought on Amazon Japan from " China-based seller · shipped from Malaysia," the other purchased on Yahoo! Auctions, Japan.

In a report over the weekend, Tibane Labs notes that the threat actor made room for the malicious circuitry by replacing the original battery with a smaller one, which powers both the implant and the Ledger X.

"Under the battery and antenna sits an ST STM32G431KBU6 (Arm Cortex‑M4, 128 KB flash, UFQFPN‑32)," the researchers found inside one of the devices.

For connectivity, the actor used "a tiny eSIM, an 8‑pad package just 2×2 mm, next to the MCU, and a shielded LTE module that sends the words out."

items.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
items.content:
GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability

GitLab warned users today to immediately patch a maximum-severity vulnerability in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances.

Tracked as CVE-2026-97229 , this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the ' joaxcar ' handle and reported via GitLab's HackerOne bug bounty program.

CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness in GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in projects' pipeline configuration files.

"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained in a Monday advisory.

GitLab fixed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.4, and 19.4 before 19.4.2, and urged users to patch their servers immediately.

"These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately," it warned. "GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action."

CVE-2026-97229 is the latest in a string of vulnerabilities that GitLab has addressed in recent months. In January, GitLab patched a high-severity two-factor authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0723 that lets attackers who know the target's account ID circumvent two-factor authentication on community and enterprise edition servers.

Last month, it addressed another maximum-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) in GitLab CE/EE that allows unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive data, such as credentials and other secrets, from vulnerable servers.

One day later, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-85706 to its catalog of flaws exploited in the wild and ordered federal agencies to secure their systems within three days.

CISA has flagged five GitLab flaws abused in attacks since November 2021, including one that was exploited by ransomware gangs.

GitLab says that over 30 million registered users and more than 50% of Fortune 100 companies use its DevSecOps platform, including Nvidia, T-Mobile, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, and Goldman Sachs.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.content:
Python 3.15 delivers a native-by-default experience on Windows on Arm

Chris Anderson, Distinguished Engineer, Windows Platform + Developer

Windows on Arm has been ready for Python development for some time. With Python 3.15 , the broader ecosystem has matured significantly, with more package maintainers publishing native Arm64 wheels, allowing Windows on Arm to support mainstream Python development across a broad and growing set of workloads.

Windows on Arm is now a Tier 2 CPython platform, backed by continuous testing and CPython’s release-quality commitments. That readiness extends beyond the runtime. Widely used packages such as NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn, Django, and FastAPI are available, while Jupyter, VS Code, Ruff, and pytest support everyday development workflows. GitHub-hosted Windows on Arm runners also let open-source maintainers build and test their projects natively.

This did not happen with a single release. Native Windows on Arm builds of CPython have been available for several versions. What changes with Python 3.15 is the maturity of the experience. Windows on Arm is now a regular CPython target; the native runtime is selected by default on Windows on Arm devices, and CPython’s Tier 2 requirements call for platform failures to be fixed or the responsible changes reverted. Package maintainers now have practical infrastructure for native Windows on Arm validation, and many widely used projects publish native Arm64 wheels. Windows on Arm is now a practical platform for many mainstream Python development scenarios. As of September 2026, a scan of the 1,000 most-downloaded PyPI projects shows about 94% of the projects’ latest releases published either a native Windows on Arm wheel or a platform-independent wheel. This measures published wheel availability, not end-to-end application compatibility. Anaconda’s main channel also includes more than 2,500 packages published for Windows on Arm .

Platform readiness does not mean every Python application is automatically ready for Windows on Arm. The runtime and a broad set of mainstream development workflows are established, but application readiness still depends on the complete dependency graph, particularly when packages rely on native extensions. Developers should confirm native Arm support for their dependencies during migration and testing.

Windows on Arm is a PEP 11 Tier 2 platform . This designation reflects a strong support commitment; the platform has reliable continuous integration and active core developers, and platform-breaking changes must be addressed promptly. Windows on Arm CI results are considered as part of CPython’s release process. This is a clear measure of how far Windows on Arm support has progressed.

Installation is now simpler. With Python Install Manager 26.4, Windows on Arm devices default to the Arm64 platform , so requesting Python 3.15 selects the native Arm64 runtime unless configuration or an explicit architecture tag overrides it.

Python 3.15 ships a complete set of Windows on Arm component packages alongside the x64 packages. CPython runs tests on Windows on Arm, including the standard interpreter and free-threaded configuration. These jobs run as part of the normal Windows build matrix.

You can confirm the architecture of the running interpreter by launching Python and inspecting its startup banner. A native Windows on Arm interpreter includes 64-bit (ARM64) in the compiler information; an x64 interpreter includes 64-bit (AMD64).

Running Python natively keeps the interpreter and native package dependencies on the same Arm64 architecture.

Applications that still depend on x64 packages can continue to run through Windows emulation, providing a practical transition path while those dependencies add native Arm support.

items.title: Y Combinator “Customer Surveillance” Startup Says “Every Company Will Soon Assign an AI Agent to Every Customer to Watch Their Every Move”.
items.content:
The secret to ensuring that your company doesn’t lose customers? Constant, AI agent-powered corporate surveillance.

That’s according to Josh Earle and Leo Paz, a pair of founders behind a vibe-coded Silicon Valley startup called Outlit. The venture argues that “AI customer surveillance” is the future of business-to-business sales. (“Our thesis,” as Earle put it in a disarmingly straightforward pitch email, is that “every company will soon assign an AI agent to every customer to watch their every move.”)

“The whole surveillance component came up because that’s the way we feel companies can serve their customers,” Earle told Futurism in an interview. “It’s really the only way we see this is going to play out.”

Outlit’s goal is to amass as much real-time information about a company’s clients as possible. According to Earle, agents trawl internal records like call logs and sales data as well as external information like social media posts and the websites of people’s employers; they then compile that data into detailed customer profiles, often complete with “actionables” like outreach recommendations and sales guidance. Outlit argues this level of insight will help companies prevent “churn” — business jargon for lost customers — or find opportunities to upsell.

“Every company is looking to automate so much customer work with agents, but there’s a whole issue of data freshness, real-time understanding of customers,” Earle said. “What we found was that if we were able to basically monitor a customer across every internal and external signal, we could actually create a real-time understanding, and this would include monitoring all the activity under product, under [customer relationship management], under LinkedIn, under website — everything.”

Outlit, which is backed by the incubator Y Combinator, is yet to be publicly released. And as it stands, it’s working mostly with business-to-business software companies, and says it isn’t in the business of monitoring individual consumers — nor does it want to be, according to Earle.

“We probably wouldn’t be going business-to-consumer,” Earle told us. “The data would suck anyway.”

But while Outlit isn’t sending agents to follow random shoppers around the web, said Earle, the goal is to “be monitoring every external data piece from a company, and the internal as well… they need to know what’s going on with [their customers] — from every call that they’ve had, from every interaction, from every LinkedIn.”

The resulting product, as described by Earle, is basically a detailed intelligence dossier.

“It’s one page, and it’s always updating,” said the founder, “and it’s all of everything we can find on them at all times.”

It’s true that companies already store a great deal of data about their clients, scouring the web for information about a given customer and its workforce; Outlit argues that there’s too much valuable data out there for individual human workers to effectively gather, let alone make sense of quickly enough for it to be relevant. But as with other AI-powered surveillance technologies, the deeply-automated process adds an extraordinary layer of scale and perpetuity to data collection and consolidation.

“A customer — let’s say a salesperson, a [customer success manager] — will wake up, they’ll go to their engine dashboard. It’ll show these cases that we built, all the contents that we pulled in, our reasoning, and what to do,” Earle explained of Outlit’s process. “Then for each customer, you can see all the sources. items.title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
items.content:
I'm going to preface this post by saying I generally don't like AI. What an original take, I know. I hate that the internet is full of slop and bots, I hate that it's used as justification to fire hundreds of thousands of workers, I hate that the AI industry is making hardware inaccessible for consumers, I hate that it's being shoved into everything, and so forth. I like to do everything by my hand and take pride in my work.

That said, every now and then there's AI news that becomes impossible to ignore or act like it doesn't matter. This is especially one of those times. AI is now able to very quickly decompile video games and software, allowing them to easily get modified and enhanced and recompiled to all sorts of different systems.

And honestly? I have to admit - it's very cool. So many old, abandoned games are getting native ports to other platforms, enhanced with high FPS and running at dynamic native resolutions, with modding support. These type of enhancements usually aren't possible through an emulator.

Decompiling games and software is the process of reverse-engineering it from a compiled version back to source code. Once decompiled, you can practically do anything you want to that code then recompile it back to an executable that runs on your computer. Or mobile phone. Or smart fridge, really.

Decompiling old games isn't a new trend. The process of picking apart an old game and re-writing the code was doable by hand, but it was so complicated and time-consuming that it took years to decompile a game. The only ones that ever make it to the finish lines are through massive community efforts. Notable decompilations tirelessly made by hand are OpenGOAL (Jak and Daxter games) and Ship of Harkinian (Zelda Ocarina of Time/Majora's Mask). These developers are legends.

Thanks to the games being decompiled, modding all these games is now possible, and there are some really fun ones. Here's Jak and Daxter but you play as Gordon from Half Life. The mod can be found here , and it was not made with AI.

Newer AI models and workflows are now able to decompile games in a matter of days, or maybe less. The code isn't nearly as clean as doing it by hand, but it works . Some ports are a mess made by people who have no idea what they're doing, but most ports are undeniably impressive and stable.

A great example of this being used for good is IsaacRecomp , which ports The Binding of Isaac in C++! No, not the remake. This is for the original Flash version made in 2011. Flash Isaac ran at a locked 30FPS and a low, blurry resolution. It was also a bit unstable because you're trying to run Adobe Flash in 2026. But now... Look at this.

The game now runs at a native 1440p, smoothly interpolated to 165FPS! If you've ever played Flash Isaac, you can immediately tell how beautiful that looks compared to the original. And it was all made automatically . In a few days. By an AI. That's insane.

There are hundreds of these projects now, with more coming every day. From a game preservation standpoint, it's incredible how we can take old janky experiences and get them to play on modern systems while also modernizing them. You can absolutely have your opinions regarding AI, but you have to admit this is cool.

Another one I like is Colin McRae Rally 2.0 , a very old game that also barely ran on modern systems. Or Final Fantasy Tactics Advance , now running at any aspect ratio with dynamic zooming in and out. There's a Metroid Prime port. There's Ratchet and Clank which should be finished soon. There are too many more to mention and I'm struggling to keep track of them all.

Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entiry tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. 매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다
